bibliographic.title: Improving reliability and accuracy of structured data extraction using a consensus large-language model approach -- a use case description in multiple sclerosis

relevance_to_mlgg: Most directly applicable paper. Multi-LLM consensus (Sonnet 3.7 + Gemini-2-pro + o3-mini) achieves 1.48% true-error rate on structured clinical data extraction, comparable to neurologist specialists (~2%). 9 rounds of prompt iteration. Method directly replicable for MLGG.
key_methods: True-error rate metric (content deviations only, not format)
19 structured variables extracted from clinical reports
key_findings: Individual LLM error rates higher; consensus overcomes ceiling effect
Prompt iteration reduced error rate from >10% to 1.48%
Format errors eliminated by structured output functions
LLM consensus comparable to medical specialist accuracy
actionable_for_mlgg: Implement dual-provider consensus: Claude + DeepSeek extract same paper, flag disagreements
Iterative prompt refinement: measure accuracy, refine SYSTEM_PROMPT, repeat
Use true-error rate (content only) as quality metric, not format errors
